rationale: This task is suitable for AsynCodeBench because PTX dialect schema and public API, operand lowering, and PTX helper rendering are natural compiler responsibilities connected as an ordered producer-consumer chain. Lowering consumes the schema's offset-capable address-slot metadata and rejection rules; rendering consumes lowering's normalized signed offsets and logical slot identities to produce collision-free helpers and valid memory-operand syntax. The public focused evaluator is meaningfully incomplete at the base with 1/12 passing and 11 intended failures, reaches 12/12 on the completed state, and has six exact role-local selectors; the selected regression evaluator reports 57 passes, while 45 optional ptxas certification cases skip because no CUDA toolkit is required for the scoped structural code-generation evidence. In private asynchronous work, lowering may use stale table metadata or rendering may assume an incompatible offset representation, causing unsupported address acceptance, helper-name collisions, or malformed PTX. The roles have local work but require both contracts for integration, so partially_parallelizable is the appropriate label.
